title: Exporting Pandas DataFrames to JSON, CSV and Dictionaries
learningObjectives: Explain the purpose of exporting pandas dataframes to json, csv and dictionaries.
Choose Pandas APIs and parameters that match the input structure.
Apply the operations to deterministic Series and DataFrames.
Validate output shape, schema, data types and missing values.
Recognize edge cases and data-quality risks.

understand.concept: Pandas writes data through to_json, to_csv and to_dict. JSON orientation determines the output structure; CSV exports should make index and encoding choices explicit. Treat exported data as an interface contract and validate field names, missing-value representation, dates and serialization format for the receiving system.
understand.whyItMatters: Reliable data workflows ingest, combine, analyze and publish structured information. Correct parsing and transformations prevent silent data loss and misleading conclusions.
understand.analogy: A DataFrame workflow is like organizing labeled records: labels and matching rules determine how records are connected.
understand.summary: Pandas writes data through to_json, to_csv and to_dict. JSON orientation determines the output structure; CSV exports should make index and encoding choices explicit. Treat exported data as an interface contract and validate field names, missing-value representation, dates and serialization format for the receiving system.

explain.narrative: This lesson explores exporting pandas dataframes to json, csv and dictionaries with small reproducible datasets. Inspect input structure before selecting parsing, join, time-frequency or export options. Validate resulting columns, row counts, index, dtypes and missing values. examples.title: Columns JSON export
examples.code:
import pandas as pd
df=pd.DataFrame({'score':[8,9]})
print(df.to_json(orient='columns'))
examples.explanation: This deterministic example demonstrates columns json export. Compare the output with the expected result and inspect the resulting data structure.

examples.title: CSV without index
examples.code:
import pandas as pd
from io import StringIO
df=pd.DataFrame({'id':[1],'qty':[3]})
out=StringIO()
df.to_csv(out,index=False)
print(out.getvalue().strip())
examples.explanation: This deterministic example demonstrates csv without index. Compare the output with the expected result and inspect the resulting data structure.

practise.guidedTask: Create a small DataFrame and complete a task related to exporting pandas dataframes to json, csv and dictionaries. Print the result and verify its schema, row count and data types.
practise.independentTask: Build a mini workflow with synthetic records. Include an edge case such as malformed input, an unmatched key, an ambiguous date or a downstream export requirement, then validate the expected result.
hints: Start with a small in-memory dataset.
Inspect columns, index and dtypes before transforming.
Make parsing, join type, time frequency or export orientation explicit.
Check row counts and duplicate keys.
Validate serialized output or read it back when practical.
practise.challenge: Add an invalid or unmatched record, handle it deliberately, and write assertions for the expected schema and row count.
validationCriteria: All five examples execute in the pinned Pandas environment.
